title: Fish Pie
subtitle: Smoked and white fish in a cream sauce under mashed potato
excerpt: Salmon, smoked haddock, and prawns poached in milk and folded into a creamy sauce with hard-boiled eggs and parsley, topped with buttery mashed potato and baked until golden.

recipe.sourceNotes: Fish pie is one of the most established British composite dishes, combining the country's tradition of pie-making with the abundance of fish from surrounding waters. The white sauce base uses the poaching milk from the fish, capturing all the flavour. Smoked haddock is almost universal, bringing a backbone of smoky depth. The combination of different textures (firm white fish, flaky smoked fish, tender prawns, and solid boiled egg) is the hallmark of the dish. Parsley and a little lemon are the standard seasoning.

recipeTools.notes: A 28 x 20 cm oven-proof dish for baking.

content.text: Poach the fish gently in milk: boiling it will make it tough and rubbery. Reserve the poaching milk to make the sauce. Do not over-stir the finished filling or the fish will break up too finely. The mash should be thick enough to spread without sinking into the filling below.

Place the salmon and smoked haddock in a wide pan. Pour over the 500 ml milk and add the bay leaves. Bring just to a simmer, then poach over low heat for 5 minutes. Remove the fish and set aside. Reserve the poaching milk. Add the prawns to the warm milk off the heat for 2 minutes until just pink. Remove and reserve.

Melt the 50 g butter in a saucepan. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the warm poaching milk, a little at a time, until you have a smooth sauce. Simmer for 5 minutes, then stir in the cream. Season. Add the parsley and lemon juice.
Flake the poached fish into large chunks. Gently fold the fish, prawns, and quartered eggs into the sauce. Tip into a baking dish.
Boil the potatoes until tender. Drain and mash with the remaining butter and warm milk. Season. Spread over the filling and rough the surface with a fork.
Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden and bubbling at the edges.
